--- a/minbpe/base.py
+++ b/minbpe/base.py
@@ -120,26 +120,21 @@
-        with open(vocab_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
-            vocab = self.vocab
-            rendered_tokens = {}
-            def render(idx):
-                if idx not in rendered_tokens:
-                    rendered_tokens[idx] = render_token(vocab[idx])
-                return rendered_tokens[idx]
-            for idx in vocab:
-                # note: many tokens may be partial utf-8 sequences
-                # and cannot be decoded into valid strings. Here we're using
-                # errors='replace' to replace them with the replacement char �.
-                # this also means that we couldn't possibly use .vocab in load()
-                # because decoding in this way is a lossy operation!
-                s = render(idx)
-                # find the children of this token, if any
-                if idx in inverted_merges:
-                    # if this token has children, render it nicely as a merge
-                    idx0, idx1 = inverted_merges[idx]
-                    s0 = render(idx0)
-                    s1 = render(idx1)
-                    f.write(f"[{s0}][{s1}] -> [{s}] {idx}\n")
-                else:
-                    # otherwise this is leaf token, just print it
-                    # (this should just be the first 256 tokens, the bytes)
-                    f.write(f"[{s}] {idx}\n")
-
+        with open(vocab_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+            vocab = self.vocab
+            rendered_tokens = {idx: render_token(token) for idx, token in vocab.items()}
+            for idx, s in rendered_tokens.items():
+                # note: many tokens may be partial utf-8 sequences
+                # and cannot be decoded into valid strings. Here we're using
+                # errors='replace' to replace them with the replacement char �.
+                # this also means that we couldn't possibly use .vocab in load()
+                # because decoding in this way is a lossy operation!
+                # find the children of this token, if any
+                if idx in inverted_merges:
+                    # if this token has children, render it nicely as a merge
+                    idx0, idx1 = inverted_merges[idx]
+                    s0 = rendered_tokens[idx0]
+                    s1 = rendered_tokens[idx1]
+                    f.write(f"[{s0}][{s1}] -> [{s}] {idx}\n")
+                else:
+                    # otherwise this is leaf token, just print it
+                    # (this should just be the first 256 tokens, the bytes)
+                    f.write(f"[{s}] {idx}\n")
+

actions.reason: Precompute rendered vocabulary strings once in Tokenizer.save and reuse them directly while writing the vocab file. This removes the per-token helper call and cache membership check in the save/load hot path while preserving the same output.

--- a/minbpe/base.py
+++ b/minbpe/base.py
@@ -119,24 +119,19 @@ class Tokenizer:
         inverted_merges = {idx: pair for pair, idx in self.merges.items()}
         with open(vocab_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
             vocab = self.vocab
-            rendered_tokens = {}
-            def render(idx):
-                if idx not in rendered_tokens:
-                    rendered_tokens[idx] = render_token(vocab[idx])
-                return rendered_tokens[idx]
-            for idx in vocab:
+            rendered_tokens = {idx: render_token(token) for idx, token in vocab.items()}
+            for idx, s in rendered_tokens.items():
                 # note: many tokens may be partial utf-8 sequences
                 # and cannot be decoded into valid strings. Here we're using
                 # errors='replace' to replace them with the replacement char �.
                 # this also means that we couldn't possibly use .vocab in load()
                 # because decoding in this way is a lossy operation!
-                s = render(idx)
                 # find the children of this token, if any
                 if idx in inverted_merges:
                     # if this token has children, render it nicely as a merge
                     idx0, idx1 = inverted_merges[idx]
-                    s0 = render(idx0)
-                    s1 = render(idx1)
+                    s0 = rendered_tokens[idx0]
+                    s1 = rendered_tokens[idx1]
                     f.write(f"[{s0}][{s1}] -> [{s}] {idx}\n")
                 else:
                     # otherwise this is leaf token, just print it
